comparison: Perfect alignment on proliferation and tumorigenesis claims (C7, C8, C49-C52, C57-C59). Both find the evidence convincing for isoform II's role in cell survival and proliferation through gain/loss-of-function and in vivo xenograft experiments.

Strong agreement on RUNX2-PRDX2 regulatory relationship (C5, C6, C87-C91, C94, C98-C103). Both accept the mechanistic link through expression correlation, ChIP-qPCR binding evidence, and partial rescue experiments. OpenEval notes incomplete rescue suggests additional mechanisms; peer reviewers satisfied after revision.

Both support ferroptosis suppression claims with overlapping evidence (C4, C60-C65, C70, C76-C77, C86). OpenEval emphasizes multiple ferroptosis markers and pharmacological rescue; peer reviewers find evidence 'convincing' for cell death via ferroptosis. OpenEval includes additional claims (C81-C84) not explicitly mentioned in peer evaluation.

Partial overlap on apoptosis claims (C55, C71-C74). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes necroptosis relies only on Nec-1 without direct markers. Peer reviewers initially raised concerns about dual ferroptosis/apoptosis roles but expressed satisfaction after revision, accepting the partial suppression through PRDX2.

Strong agreement on HOXA10/RUNX2/PRDX2 pathway (C115, C117-C122, C126-C135). Both accept the upstream regulatory relationship and rescue experiments. OpenEval provides detailed systematic analysis; peer reviewers describe it as 'novel mechanism' and 'valuable insight' with satisfaction after addressing dual cell death pathway concerns.

Overlap on HOXA10 upstream regulation (C9-C11, C105, C107-C109, C114). OpenEval supports isoform-specific knockdown effects and correlation analysis; peer reviewers accept as part of the novel HOXA10/RUNX2/PRDX2 mechanism. Peer evaluation includes broader pathway claims not in OpenEval R6.

Agreement on HOXA10 clinical expression and correlation data (C110-C113). OpenEval finds upstream regulatory relationship supported; peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of critique and acceptance of overall pathway mechanism.

Agreement on clinical correlation and prognostic data (C12-C14, C36, C38-C39, C41, C47). OpenEval emphasizes TCGA analysis, clinical validation, and survival analysis; peer reviewers implicitly accept clinical relevance through statement about 'valuable insight' into RUNX2's role in OSCC. OpenEval includes additional pan-cancer claims not addressed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R1 includes pan-cancer expression data (C42-C46) that peer R7 accepts without critique. Both support broader significance of isoform II beyond OSCC, though peer evaluation is implicit through lack of concerns rather than explicit endorsement.

Perfect agreement on in vivo PRDX2 validation (C92-C93). Both accept xenograft data as crucial validation that PRDX2 mediates isoform II's oncogenic effects. OpenEval explicitly parallels with isoform II knockdown results; peer reviewers accept as part of PRDX2-mediated mechanism.

Perfect agreement on differential migration/invasion effects (C53-C54). Both accept that isoform II's role is primarily in proliferation/survival rather than metastasis. OpenEval notes only overexpression tested; peer reviewers raise no concerns about these findings.

Overlap on RSL3 sensitivity experiments (C81-C84). OpenEval includes these as part of ferroptosis suppression evidence; peer reviewers implicitly accept as functional validation of ferroptosis mechanism through their acceptance of 'convincing evidence' for cell death mechanisms.

Perfect agreement on mitochondrial morphology claims (C66-C69). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic link and lack of FIS1 rescue experiments; peer reviewers accept without critique, suggesting implicit support for the descriptive findings if not the proposed mechanism.

Perfect agreement on negative TFRC results (C95-C97). Both accept that isoform II does not affect iron transport, supporting mechanism through antioxidant pathways rather than iron metabolism. OpenEval emphasizes importance of negative result; peer reviewers accept through lack of concerns.

Perfect agreement on GPX4 regulation (C156-C157). Both support that isoform II regulates GPX4 alongside PRDX2. OpenEval notes uncertainty about direct vs. indirect regulation; peer reviewers accept as consistent with overall antioxidant mechanism without raising concerns.

Overlap on combination rescue experiments (C75, C123). OpenEval includes C75 in apoptosis evaluation; peer R14 specifically highlights these additive effects as addressing reviewer concerns about relative contributions of ferroptosis and apoptosis. Both support the findings after revision.

Minimal overlap on 4-HNE staining (C85). OpenEval includes as part of comprehensive ferroptosis marker evidence; peer reviewers accept as in vivo validation of lipid peroxidation consistent with ferroptosis mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates basal apoptosis claim (C56) as SUPPORTED, noting isoform II maintains survival under stress rather than suppressing basal apoptosis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this negative result may not have been specifically discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims (C1-C2, C15-C22) as SUPPORTED, providing context for the study. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these established background claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates additional background claims about RUNX2 isoforms and cancer (C3, C23-C34) as SUPPORTED through citations. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these contextual claims from prior literature.

OpenEval evaluates discussion background claims (C136-C142, C145-C153) as SUPPORTED through appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these literature-based contextual claims that support the rationale and interpretation.

OpenEval R17 evaluates summary/conclusion claims (C143-C144, C154-C155, C158) as SUPPORTED by collective evidence. Peer R1 includes C143 as part of ferroptosis/apoptosis evaluation, accepting the dual mechanism conclusion. Peer R2 and R3 include C144 and C154-C155 respectively as part of pathway mechanism acceptance.
OpenEval R17's summary claim C144 about PRDX2 as mediator overlaps with peer R2's acceptance of the RUNX2-PRDX2 regulatory relationship. Both support this as a key finding of the study.

OpenEval R17's summary claims C154-C155 about the complete pathway overlap with peer R3's acceptance of the 'novel mechanism of HOXA10/RUNX2/PRDX2 control.' Both support the integrated pathway as the main conclusion.
